title: A henselian local ring as a directed colimit of henselian local G-rings
statement: Let $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ be a commutative henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$ (a preordered set in which any two indices have a common upper bound), commutative henselian local Noetherian G-rings $(A_i,\mathfrak m_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], ring maps $u_{ji}:A_i\to A_j$ for $i\le j$, and compatible ring maps $u_i:A_i\to C$, with identity and composition laws $u_{ii}=1$, $u_{ki}=u_{kj}u_{ji}$ and $u_j u_{ji}=u_i$, such that every map is local: $u_{ji}^{-1}(\mathfrak m_j)=\mathfrak m_i$ and $u_i^{-1}(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_i$. The cocone $(C,(u_i))$ is a colimit of the $A_i$ in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Neither the transition maps nor the maps to $C$ are required to be injective.

source.place: Tag 0A41, label lemma-henselian-local-limit-G-rings, statement and proof; G-ring includes Noetherianity. The construction localizes finitely generated integer subalgebras at the contracted maximal ideal and takes ordinary henselizations; local cocone maps follow their local universal property.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-colimit-essentially-finite-type-over-z] to the local ring $C$. Obtain a nonempty directed set $I$, local rings $(R_i,\mathfrak n_i)$ essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, local transition maps $r_{ji}$, and local maps $\pi_i:R_i\to C$, exhibiting $C$ as their colimit in commutative rings. The indices form a set, not a proper class, so this is a small diagram. Here and below use the colimit universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 0A41, lemma-henselian-local-limit-G-rings, first three sentences of the proof; the localized base system is the one supplied by Algebra Tag 00QU, lemma-limit-essentially-finite-type, proof

proof.text: For each $i$, the meaning of essentially finite type in [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] supplies a finitely generated integer algebra $B_i$, a multiplicative subset $W_i\subset B_i$, and an isomorphism $R_i\cong L_i:=W_i^{-1}B_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-g-ring], $B_i$ is a G-ring and hence Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], $L_i$ is Noetherian. We next check its G-ring condition directly, rather than taking the essentially-finite-type case from a node that only states the finite-type case.

source.place: Tag 0A41, proof: the localized rings are Noetherian G-rings; Proposition Tag 07PX, proposition-ubiquity-G-ring, and Proposition Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, opening localization argument

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q\subset L_i$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be its inverse image in $B_i$. No element of $W_i$ lies in $\mathfrak p$, because its image is a unit. For a fraction $b/w$, membership in $\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to $b\in\mathfrak p$, since $w/1$ is a unit. Thus the maps on fractions give inverse local ring isomorphisms $(L_i)_{\mathfrak q}\cong(B_i)_{\mathfrak p}$: send $(b/w)/(c/v)$ to $bv/(wc)$, where $c\notin\mathfrak p$, and send $b/c$ back to $(b/1)/(c/1)$. They are well defined by the localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property], since exactly the required denominators become units; their composites fix all numerators and inverted denominators. They identify maximal ideals, as the displayed membership criterion shows. This is just iterated localization at a prime, with prime localizations as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, first sentence of proof; elementary fraction verification of the prime-localization identification

proof.text: The G-ring condition on $B_i$ says that $(B_i)_{\mathfrak p}\to\widehat{(B_i)_{\mathfrak p}}$ is regular. The local ring isomorphism in step 3 identifies the maximal ideals. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-ring-equiv] to obtain the corresponding isomorphism of completions, commuting with the completion maps. Then [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-map-ring-equiv] makes $(L_i)_{\mathfrak q}\to\widehat{(L_i)_{\mathfrak q}}$ regular. This holds for every prime $\mathfrak q$; together with Noetherianity from step 2, [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] proves that $L_i$ is a G-ring. Transport along $L_i\cong R_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-ring-equiv]. Thus every $R_i$ is a Noetherian local G-ring.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, opening localization argument; Definition Tag 07GH, definition-G-ring

proof.text: The maps $r_{ji}$ carry $\mathfrak n_i$ into $\mathfrak n_j$ by their localness. In fact $\pi_i^{-1}(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak n_i$: the forward inclusion for $\mathfrak n_i$ is given, and an element outside $\mathfrak n_i$ is a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], hence maps to a unit and lies outside $\mathfrak m_C$. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](1), every $c\in C$ is $\pi_i(x)$ for some $i,x$. If $c\in\mathfrak m_C$, the preceding equality puts $x\in\mathfrak n_i$. Conversely all $\pi_i(\mathfrak n_i)$ lie in $\mathfrak m_C$. Therefore $\mathfrak m_C=\bigcup_i\pi_i(\mathfrak n_i)$, and $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ is exactly the directed colimit pair to which the henselization-colimit theorem applies.

source.place: Tag 0A41, proof, application of Tag 0A04, lemma-henselization-colimit; verification of its colimit-ideal hypothesis

proof.text: Let $(A_i,\mathfrak a_i)$ be the henselization of $(R_i,\mathfrak n_i)$ from [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], with structure map $\eta_i$ and $\mathfrak a_i=\mathfrak n_iA_i$. This node states both that the pair is henselian and that $A_i/\mathfrak a_i\cong R_i/\mathfrak n_i$. The latter is a nonzero field. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion], $\mathfrak a_i$ is in every maximal ideal of $A_i$. Since it is itself maximal (the quotient is a field), it is the unique maximal ideal. Thus put $\mathfrak m_i=\mathfrak a_i$; $A_i$ is henselian local in the terminology of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-pair-g-ring] to the G-ring $R_i$ and ideal $\mathfrak n_i$ to see that $A_i$ is a G-ring, in particular Noetherian. This uses pair henselization throughout, so no unstated comparison with a second construction of ordinary henselization is needed.

source.place: Tag 0A41, final sentence of proof; Tag 0AH3, lemma-henselization-pair-G-ring, together with Tag 0A02, lemma-henselization, quotient and henselian-pair clauses, and Tags 09XE/09XI for the Jacobson-radical clause

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-colimit] to the directed system $(R_i,\mathfrak n_i)$, the ring colimit $C$, and the ideal equality of step 5. Its clause (1) gives maps $u_{ji}:A_i\to A_j$ extending $r_{ji}$, preserving the extended ideals, and satisfying the identity and composition laws. Its henselian specialization applies because $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ is henselian by hypothesis. It supplies compatible maps $u_i:A_i\to C$ extending $\pi_i$, preserving the extended ideals, and inducing an isomorphism $\varinjlim_i A_i\cong C$. Since this isomorphism is induced by these very $u_i$, it exhibits $(C,(u_i))$ as a colimit cocone in commutative rings, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 0A41, proof: A = colim A_i^h by Tag 0A04, lemma-henselization-colimit; henselian specialization of its pair form

proof.text: It remains to verify the stated inverse-image equalities. Step 7 gives $u_{ji}(\mathfrak m_i)\subseteq\mathfrak m_j$ and $u_i(\mathfrak m_i)\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$. If $a\notin\mathfrak m_i$, it is a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion]. Its image under either ring map is a unit, hence outside the target maximal ideal by the same criterion. This proves $u_{ji}^{-1}(\mathfrak m_j)=\mathfrak m_i$ and $u_i^{-1}(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_i$. All identity, composition, compatibility and colimit assertions were proved in step 7, and step 6 gives all the asserted properties of the rings. At no point was injectivity of the henselized maps used or asserted.

source.place: Tag 0A41, local-transition assertion; explicit unit check also gives localness of the cocone maps

Step 2 checks Noetherianity from the essentially-finite-type definition, 07PX for finite-type Z-algebras and the localization-Noetherian lemma; it does not use the finite-type-only node for the localized case. Step 3: I checked that the iterated-localization isomorphism (W^{-1}B)_q = B_p is well defined; it rests on 00CP's existence and uniqueness. Step 4 moves the G-ring property along this isomorphism with the completion-iso and regular-map-iso nodes. Step 5 shows m_C = union of pi_i(n_i) using the unit criterion and the elementwise filtered-colimit lemma, which is exactly the ideal I that the 0A04 node needs. Step 6 shows the pair henselization of (R_i, n_i) is henselian local: its quotient is a field and 09XI(i) puts that ideal in the Jacobson radical. 0AH3 then makes it a G-ring. Step 7: the henselian part of the 0A04 node gives the unique compatible beta_i and an isomorphism from the colimit, so (C, beta_i) is a colimit cocone. Step 8 gets the inverse-image equalities from the unit criterion. Small cases: C a field, C non-Noetherian, and non-injective maps are all fine. There is no cycle (DFS over 908 ancestors) and no duplicate of 0A41. Every step's citations match its uses. I accept the 11 declared tool uses as generic commutative-algebra black boxes. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_henselianLocal_isGRing_colimit (C : Type u) [CommRing C] [HenselianLocalRing C] : ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (π : F ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj (CommRingCat.of C)), (∀ i : I, HenselianLocalRing (F.obj i)) ∧ (∀ i : I, IsNoetherianRing (F.obj i)) ∧ (∀ i : I, IsGRing (F.obj i)) ∧ (∀ (i j : I) (f : i ⟶ j), IsLocalHom (F.map f).hom) ∧ (∀ i : I, IsLocalHom (π.app i).hom) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk (CommRingCat.of C) π))
